newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER SHOWCASE-FEYENOORD-AJAX GAME SWITCHED TO AFTERNOON.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-FEYENOORD-AJAX GAME SWITCHED TO AFTERNOON.

text.p: Sunday's Dutch first division soccer match between Feyenoord and Ajax Amsterdam has been brought forward to 2.30pm (1330 GMT) from the scheduled 6.00pm (1700 GMT) start, the Dutch ANP news agency said on Thursday.
Rotterdam mayor Bram Peper said on Tuesday he wanted the game brought forward so police could more easily control supporters during daylight hours.
As mayor, Peper is chief of the Rotterdam police and can introduce special decrees if he thinks public order may be disrupted.
Late on Wednesday he effectively banned the game from kicking off in the evening, leaving the Dutch soccer association (KNVB) little option but to accept the move.
Police expect up to 50,000 fans, including 1,600 Ajax supporters, to attend the game, one of the classics of the Dutch soccer calendar.
The two clubs have a history of hooliganism and around 400 police will be drafted in to maintain order on match day.
The KNVB had initially opposed switching the kick-off time, saying Rotterdam police had okayed the schedule at the start of the season.
A KNVB spokesman earlier denied this stance had anything to do with plans of a new sports-only TV channel Sport7, in which the KNVB has a stake, to broadcast the evening match live.
